title: Dover vs MarketerHire (August 2026)
summary: Compare Dover vs MarketerHire for marketing talent in August 2026. Dover builds permanent teams (~$2K-8K/hire) while MarketerHire rents freelancers
body_markdown:
When you’re looking for[marketing talent](https://www.dover.com/) , the choice often comes down to hiring freelancers or building an in-house team. MarketerHire and Dover take very different approaches: MarketerHire connects you with freelance marketers, while Dover gives you access to fractional recruiters who help you build your own full-time team. At its core, the decision is about whether you want to rent expertise or invest in long-term capabilities, and both paths come with trade-offs that founders often overlook. This post offers a framework to help you choose the right fit for your team.


**TLDR:**


-


Fractional recruiting services help you hire full-time employees, while talent marketplaces like MarketerHire rent pre-vetted freelancers on monthly subscriptions.


-


MarketerHire works well for part-time roles or 3-6 month projects; fractional recruiting services build permanent internal marketing skills over time.


-


Fractional recruiting services can hire across all roles, including marketing specialists, engineering, and sales.


-


Marketers hired through a recruiting service integrate with your culture and long-term strategy; freelancers remain external contractors.


-


Per-hire costs for fractional recruiting services average $2,000 to $7,000, compared to $5,000 or more per month for talent marketplace subscriptions.


## What MarketerHire Does and Their Approach


MarketerHire is a freelance talent marketplace that matches businesses with pre-vetted marketing professionals. Unlike traditional freelance marketplaces, it acts as a curated matching service, specializing only in marketing roles like SEO, paid ads, content, and email marketing.


They use specific information to find someone in their network who has already solved that exact type of problem for businesses like yours. They don’t just match keywords. They look for relevant experience and fit.


MarketerHire uses a tiered subscription model: $5,000/month for Starter (single-channel), around $10,000/month for Growth (multi-channel), and $15,000+ for Scale-level support. You get one recommended marketer with a background summary and fit rationale, and the service runs on monthly retainers instead of recruiting fees.


The approach focuses solely on marketing talent, which means deep expertise in that specific area. But it also means you’re limited to marketing roles when your hiring needs likely extend beyond just marketing specialists.


## What Dover Does and Our Approach


Dover takes a different approach by focusing on recruiting help across all roles. Instead of providing the actual talent, we help you build your own team through[fractional recruiters](https://www.dover.com/blog/what-is-a-fractional-recruiter) who work as extensions of your hiring process.


Dover Recruiting Partners are vetted fractional recruiters who can work as an extension of your team. Dover maintains a[highly selective network of experienced recruiters](https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M14-dover-recruiting-partners) with deep startup hiring backgrounds. Dover combines a[free ATS for startups](https://www.dover.com/ats) with access to those recruiters to help companies hire across all roles, including marketing and beyond.


Fractional recruiters work best when both the recruiter and the hiring team have real-time visibility into the same candidate pipeline. Without a shared system, coordination can break down fast: duplicate outreach, unclear handoffs, and feedback that never reaches the recruiter. Pairing an ATS with a fractional recruiter from the start gives both sides a single place to track sourcing, screening, and hiring manager notes, cutting the overhead that slows most early-stage hiring processes.


Dover’s marketplace operates as the infrastructure layer that fractional recruiting agencies are built on. Each recruiter in the network carries verified reviews from past clients, giving you direct insight into their hiring track record before you start. That visibility is rarely available through traditional agencies, where recruiter quality is typically taken on faith.


The cost per hire across our marketplace varies, but it averages between $2,000 and $7,000. Dover’s model focuses on helping companies build their own teams by providing recruiting expertise and tools, instead of supplying the actual talent like MarketerHire does.


Dover’s fractional recruiters work with companies to source, screen, and hire full-time employees across engineering, sales, marketing, operations, and executive roles. The service includes strategic hiring support, process development, and candidate pipeline management through Dover’s integrated recruiting technology.


> Dover’s approach creates lasting value by helping you build internal teams rather than providing temporary solutions that require ongoing monthly payments.


Our fractional recruiters integrate directly with your team, attending meetings, developing hiring strategies, and adjusting approaches based on your evolving needs. They bring the strategic thinking of talent acquisition specialists while providing the tactical execution of experienced recruiters.


The key difference is ownership. Dover helps you hire people who become part of your company, contribute to your culture, and grow with your business over time.


## When to use MarketerHire vs Dover


MarketerHire is best for companies that don’t have time to vet freelancers and want to work with senior-level marketers who can start delivering right away. Their model works well for short-term marketing projects, specific campaign needs, or when you need immediate marketing support without the commitment of hiring full-time staff.


MarketerHire makes sense for 3-6 month projects or testing new marketing channels without a permanent hire. The tradeoff is a minimum $5,000/month commitment.


Dover is the better choice when you’re looking to hire full-time employees, build your internal team, or need recruiting help across multiple roles.


When[recruiting consumes 30-50% of your time](https://a16zcrypto.com/posts/article/why-startups-should-hire-recruiters/) , Dover helps you hire the right people instead of renting them temporarily. See our guide on[when to hire your first recruiter](https://www.dover.com/blog/when-startups-hire-fractional-recruiter) if you’re unsure.


Scenario MarketerHire Dover


Building internal marketing team ❌ Expensive long-term ✅ Best choice


Hiring across multiple roles ❌ Marketing only ✅ All roles covered


6+ month marketing needs ❌ Gets expensive ✅ Better ROI


The basic question is whether you want to rent marketing expertise or build internal marketing skills. MarketerHire provides the former, while Dover allows the latter.


## Cost Considerations and Longterm Value


With MarketerHire, you pay the monthly fee indefinitely without building internal skills. If cost is your main driver, a full-time marketer often delivers better consistency and strategic depth.


Dover’s cost per hire averages $2,000 to $7,000, building internal marketing capacity instead of requiring ongoing monthly payments. For a detailed breakdown, see[hourly recruiting vs. agency fees](https://www.dover.com/blog/contingency-vs-hourly-recruiting-costs) .


Beyond cost, the real distinction is **strategic vs. tactical value** . MarketerHire freelancers execute short-term campaigns but remain external. Dover’s recruiters help you hire full-time marketers who build institutional knowledge and grow with your company over time.


A $5,000 Starter subscription costs $60,000 per year, climbing to $120,000+ at Growth or Scale tiers. For context,[SHRM’s 2025 benchmarking report](https://www.shrm.org/about/press-room/shrm-releases-2025-benchmarking-reports--how-does-your-organizat) puts the average cost per hire at $5,475 for non-executive roles. Dover’s average per-hire costs of $2,000-$7,000 build internal capacity that grows with your business.[Dover’s recruiting model](https://www.dover.com/blog/five-reasons-why-recruiting-is-uniquely-suited-for-a-fractional-model) builds in accountability by keeping fractional recruiters focused on long-term outcomes.


## Why Dover Is the Better Solution for Full-Time Hires


Dover tackles the fundamental challenge that MarketerHire cannot solve: building your own team. While MarketerHire has its merits for fractional and part-time marketing needs, it’s not designed for long-term hires or building internal skills.


Fractional workers, typically highly skilled professionals, seek variety in their projects.[McKinsey research on the gig economy](https://www.mckinsey.com/featured-insights/mckinsey-explainers/what-is-the-gig-economy) puts gig and freelance participation at nearly 36% of the U.S. workforce, with demand growing in areas like marketing, finance, HR, and executive leadership. While fractional marketing talent serves immediate needs, growing companies need internal skills.


Dover Recruiting Partners gives you access to top-tier recruiting talent without the long-term commitment or exorbitant fees. Our[fractional recruiting model](https://www.dover.com/blog/fractional-recruiting-guide) allows you to work with a separate expert recruiter for each role you’re hiring for, whether it’s a senior engineer, a sales leader, or a product manager.


This approach scales with your hiring needs rather than locking you into monthly marketing subscriptions. For example, your[first sales rep hiring](https://www.dover.com/blog/how-to-hire-your-first-sales-rep) becomes much easier when you have experienced recruiting support rather than trying to figure it out yourself.


## FAQs


### What’s the main difference between Dover and MarketerHire?


MarketerHire provides pre-vetted freelance marketers on monthly subscriptions starting at $5,000 (with Growth and Scale tiers reaching $10,000 to $15,000+/month), while Dover offers fractional recruiters who help you hire full-time employees across all roles. Average hiring costs per role land around $2,000-$7,000.


### Do I need an ATS before bringing in a fractional recruiter?


Not always, but having one makes the engagement work more cleanly. A shared ATS gives both the recruiter and your internal team real-time pipeline visibility, which cuts coordination overhead and prevents duplicate outreach. Dover pairs its recruiter network with a free ATS so both layers are set up and connected from the start, with no separate software contract needed.


### What are the best hiring tools for YC-backed startups?


YC-backed startups need hiring tools that move fast without a full-time recruiter. Dover pairs a free ATS with on-demand fractional recruiters who have deep startup backgrounds, and is used by 100+ YC companies across all roles. For short-term marketing needs, MarketerHire offers pre-vetted freelancers on monthly subscriptions. Dover fits teams building a permanent cross-functional team; MarketerHire fits time-boxed marketing projects.


### What hiring tools do YC startups typically use?


Many YC startups pair a lightweight ATS with on-demand recruiting support. Dover is used by 100+ YC-backed companies, covering sourcing, screening, and closing across all roles. Some use MarketerHire for immediate channel or campaign support. The most common pattern: Dover for building a permanent team, MarketerHire for short-term marketing work.


## Final Thoughts on Choosing Between Dover and MarketerHire


The decision between Dover and MarketerHire comes down to whether you want to build lasting marketing skills or solve immediate needs. MarketerHire works well for short-term projects, but Dover creates compound value by helping you hire marketers who grow with your business. If you’re planning to scale your team beyond just marketing, Dover gives you[fractional recruiters](https://www.dover.com/recruiters) that provide expertise to hire across all roles. For most companies scaling past one or two roles, building an internal team tends to create more durable value than ongoing rental fees.
